device.category: duophonic analogue synthesizer: two expander modules in one desktop / Eurorack (80 HP) case
device.based_on: Oberheim Two Voice, which paired two SEMs (Synthesizer Expander Modules). The guide never names Oberheim; the module name, the notch-sweeping 12 dB state-variable filter and the bipolar mix controls are the SEM's.

sources.title: 2-XM Quick Start Guide
sources.note: 108 numbered controls on pages 22 to 23 (1 to 28 for XM1, 29 to 56 for XM2, 70 to 85 and 86 to 101 for the two patchbays), a poly chain note and a specifications table. Unusually for a quick start guide it gives envelope times and the LFO range.

architecture.polyphony_mode: duophonic: unison, split or duo across the two modules; poly chain across units
architecture.summary: Two complete, independent synthesizer voices side by side, each with its own panel: two VCOs with sawtooth and pulse (VCO2 syncable to VCO1), a bipolar modulation knob per VCO that gives frequency modulation one way and pulse width modulation the other, a 12 dB/octave multimode filter whose NOTCH knob sweeps continuously from low-pass through notch to high-pass (or switches to band-pass), bipolar crossfade controls that mix each VCO's saw against its pulse and external audio against white noise, two ADS envelopes, an LFO and a VCA. Each module has a 16-jack patchbay. A master section sets each module's level, pan, external input level and portamento, and assigns the two voices as unison, split or duo.

modules.name: Voice assignment
modules.description: Receives MIDI and hands notes to the two modules. UNISON: both play one note; a second note goes to one module by the priority set in SynthTRIBE (highest, lowest or last for XM1, XM2 takes the other). SPLIT: XM1 below the split point (default C4), XM2 above, XM2 on the next MIDI channel up. DUO: both modules on one channel duophonically, or on separate channels. Also produces each module's MIDI-derived CV, gate and velocity.

modules.name: White noise
modules.description: White noise source reached through each module's EXT crossfade control. Shared between the modules by inference; the guide does not say.

modules.name: A440 tuning reference
modules.description: A fixed 440 Hz tone that replaces the external input when nothing is patched into a module's EXT jack, for tuning.

modules.name: Master output
modules.description: Sums the two modules with their own level and pan into a stereo pair, then master volume, to the 3.5 mm stereo jack on top and two 6.35 mm jacks on the rear.

modules.name: XM1 pitch
modules.description: Takes this module's MIDI pitch through portamento, and the two pitch patch points. VCO1 CV drives VCO1, and VCO2 as well unless VCO2 CV is patched.

modules.name: XM1 envelope gate
modules.description: Gate that fires both envelopes: MIDI by default, ENV GATE jack when patched.

modules.name: XM1 VCO 1
modules.description: Sawtooth and pulse, both always running, mixed into the filter by a bipolar crossfade. Coarse tuning over five octaves, fine tuning, pulse width 10 to 90%. One bipolar MODULATION knob: counter-clockwise frequency modulation, clockwise pulse width modulation, from the source on its switch.

modules.name: XM1 VCO 2
modules.description: Sawtooth and pulse, both always running, mixed into the filter by a bipolar crossfade. Coarse tuning over five octaves, fine tuning, pulse width 10 to 90%. One bipolar MODULATION knob: counter-clockwise frequency modulation, clockwise pulse width modulation, from the source on its switch. Syncable to VCO1.

modules.name: XM1 LFO
modules.description: LFO, 0.1 to 55 Hz, one rate control, retriggerable from the LFO TRIG jack. Shape not stated.

modules.name: XM1 ENV 1 (VCA)
modules.description: Attack, decay, sustain envelope for the VCA and VCO1's modulation. DECAY also sets release. Times are specified.

modules.name: XM1 ENV 2
modules.description: Attack, decay, sustain envelope for the filter and VCO2's modulation. DECAY also sets release.

modules.name: XM1 VCF
modules.description: 12 dB/octave multimode filter. With RESPONSE at LP-HP, the NOTCH knob sweeps continuously from low-pass (fully counter-clockwise) through a notch (centre) to high-pass (fully clockwise); at BP it is band-pass. Inputs are the two VCO crossfades and the external/noise crossfade. Bipolar modulation depth from ENV 2, an external CV or velocity, or the LFO.

modules.name: XM1 VCA
modules.description: Output amplifier, driven by ENV 1, by ENV 1 scaled by velocity, or held open (ON/EXT), in which case a CV in VCA CV takes control.

modules.name: XM2 pitch
modules.description: Takes this module's MIDI pitch through portamento, and the two pitch patch points. VCO1 CV drives VCO1, and VCO2 as well unless VCO2 CV is patched.

indicators.label: Power
indicators.function: Power indicator. Turns red when poly chain is enabled; its normal colour is not stated.

led_legend.rule: One LED. Red means poly chain is enabled.
led_legend.note: From the poly chaining paragraph. The normal colour is not given.

behaviours.name: Two independent voices
behaviours.rule: XM1 and XM2 are complete, separately-controlled voices, not two instances of one patch. The ASSIGN switch sets how notes reach them: UNISON (both on one note), SPLIT (XM1 low, XM2 high, split at C4 by default, XM2 on the next MIDI channel) or DUO (one note each, same or separate channels). Each module has its own level and pan.

behaviours.name: Bipolar VCO modulation
behaviours.rule: Each VCO's MODULATION knob does nothing at 12 o'clock, frequency modulation as it turns counter-clockwise and pulse width modulation as it turns clockwise, from the source on its switch. VCO1's switch offers ENV 1, ENV 1 x velocity or the LFO; VCO2's offers ENV 2, ENV 2 x velocity or the LFO. Recorded with amount_expr on the connections.

behaviours.name: Bipolar mix crossfades
behaviours.rule: There are no level knobs in the usual sense. VCO 1 and VCO 2 each crossfade saw (counter-clockwise) against pulse (clockwise) with silence at 12 o'clock; EXT crossfades the external input against white noise the same way.

behaviours.name: Notch-sweeping filter
behaviours.rule: A 12 dB/octave state-variable filter. At LP-HP, NOTCH morphs the response: fully counter-clockwise low-pass, centre a narrow notch, fully clockwise high-pass; between them the notch widens or narrows. BP switches to band-pass. This continuous mode sweep is the defining sound of the SEM.

behaviours.name: Velocity through E+V
behaviours.rule: The middle position of the VCO modulation, VCA and filter modulation switches scales the envelope by MIDI velocity. On the filter this position is labelled EXT: a CV in the VCF CV jack replaces the velocity-scaled envelope.

behaviours.name: VCA ON/EXT
behaviours.rule: At ON/EXT the VCA is held fully open, making the module a drone, unless a CV is patched into VCA CV, which then controls it.

behaviours.name: A440 tuning tone
behaviours.rule: With nothing in a module's EXT jack, its external input carries a 440 Hz reference tone, heard through the EXT crossfade and the module's EXT LVL. Useful for tuning, and a surprise if the EXT knob is not centred.

behaviours.name: Pitch normalling
behaviours.rule: MIDI pitch drives both VCOs. VCO1 CV replaces it for VCO1 and also for VCO2 unless VCO2 CV is patched, so one cable plays both oscillators and a second separates them.

behaviours.name: ADS envelopes
behaviours.rule: Attack 3 ms to 6 s. DECAY sets decay (14 ms to 18 s) and release (10 ms to 15 s) together. Sustain level.

behaviours.name: Poly chain
behaviours.rule: Units with the same MIDI channel and poly chain on in SynthTRIBE pass unhandled notes down the chain; the first unit plays the first note and so on. With poly chain on in the last unit, notes beyond the chain are dropped; with it off, the last unit steals its last note. The guide adds that a 2-XM in paraphonic mode handles two notes, without describing a paraphonic mode.

channel.set_by: rear DIP switches or SynthTRIBE; XM2 uses channel + 1 in split

source_inconsistencies: CV 1 and CV 2 are printed in the IN column of each patchbay but the guide lists them as outputs (77, 93).
The VCF modulation source middle position is EXT on the panel and 'External/ENV2 controlled by MIDI velocity' in the guide.
Item 24 refers the VCF modulation knob to 'switches 22 & 52'; the switches are 24 and 52.
The specifications list the filters as '2 LPF 12 dB/octave'; the controls describe low-pass, notch, high-pass and band-pass.

Items 63 and 68 say 'Where no external source is present a tuning tone of A 440 Hz will be heard' and item 28 says it 'will be routed'; consistent in meaning, but the level control and the crossfade both claim it.
Item 73 contains the typo 'no jack ios inserted'.

modelling_gaps.detail: The notch sweep is described qualitatively. No cutoff range, resonance law, or statement of how the notch width maps to the knob.
Envelope and LFO end points are given; the mapping from knob position to time or rate is not.
Modelled with amount_expr as max(0, -x) and max(0, x). The actual crossfade law (linear, equal-power, overlap at centre) is not stated.
No Oberheim SEM or Two Voice documentation was supplied; it would settle filter behaviour and the VCO output waveforms.
